one_line_description.value: WooCommerce is an open-source eCommerce platform built on WordPress for selling physical products, digital downloads, subscriptions, content, and appointments.
one_line_description.quote: WooCommerce is a customizable, open-source eCommerce platform built on WordPress.

has_public_api.quote: WooCommerce (WC) 2.6+ is fully integrated with the WordPress REST API.

api_type.quote: Use the REST API for store management data. Use the Store API for shopper-facing product, cart, and checkout flows.

api_breadth.value: REST, read-write; core resources include orders, products, coupons, customers, and shipping zones, plus webhooks and a separate unauthenticated shopper-facing Store API
api_breadth.quote: The WC REST API is a powerful part of WooCommerce which lets you read and write various parts of WooCommerce data such as orders, products, coupons, customers, and shipping zones.

auth_methods.quote: For Authorization, choose basic auth and enter your consumer key and consumer secret keys from WooCommerce into the username and password fields.

oauth_scopes_documented.quote: WooCommerce includes two ways to authenticate with the WP REST API.

access_model.quote: The WooCommerce REST API uses a key system to control access. You can create keys with different permission levels depending on what the connected application needs.

access_notes.value: Free, open-source core plugin: a store admin self-generates a consumer key/secret under WooCommerce > Settings > Advanced > REST API with Read, Write, or Read/Write permission - no vendor approval, plan tier, or app review is involved. The practical gate is that the developer must run their own WordPress + WooCommerce store (or a local dev store via Studio CLI/wp-env) with pretty permalinks enabled. Separate products are gated: Woo Marketplace SaaS Billing API requires business review before sandbox credentials are issued, and the MCP integration is a developer preview requiring the WordPress MCP Adapter plugin plus a WordPress Application Password.
access_notes.quote: This documentation is about the free, core WooCommerce plugin, for which support is provided in our community forums on WordPress.org.

official_mcp_server.quote: WooCommerce abilities are available through the WordPress MCP Adapter's default server:

rate_limits.value: Not documented for the core WC REST API v3; Store API rate limiting is optional and disabled by default, but when enabled the default maximum is 25 requests per 10 seconds, and the checkout/place-order flow can be limited to 3 requests per 60 seconds
rate_limits.quote: A default maximum of 25 requests can be made within a 10-second time frame.

webhooks.quote: The webhooks API allows you to create, view, update, and delete individual, or a batch, of webhooks.

sandbox_or_test_env.quote: Studio starts the local site and gives you its URL.

sdk_languages.quote: JavaScript Library - PHP Library - Python Library - Ruby Library

api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.value: URL-namespaced versioning under /wp-json/wc/v3/ (current integration version is v3); the legacy REST API has been removed from WooCommerce core and old integrations require the separate WooCommerce Legacy REST API plugin
api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.quote: The legacy REST API has been removed from WooCommerce core.

verdict_reason: WooCommerce exposes a documented, versioned REST API (/wp-json/wc/v3/) covering read-write access to orders, products, coupons, customers, shipping zones, and webhooks, with official JavaScript/PHP/Python/Ruby libraries. Credentials are self-serve: a store admin generates a consumer key/secret with chosen permissions in the WP admin, with no app review, plan tier, or sales contact required. The only practical requirement is running your own WordPress + WooCommerce store or a local dev store.
open_questions: Auth: the llms-full.txt content states 'You must use OAuth 1.0a "one-legged" authentication' for authentication over HTTP; this was not included in auth_methods because the dedicated authentication page describes only REST API keys and the Application Authentication endpoint - confirm whether OAuth 1.0a should be listed (likely as 'other').
OAuth scopes: no OAuth2 flow or scope list is documented; the auth-endpoint 'scope' parameter refers to read/write/read_write key permission level, so oauth_scopes_documented was set to false.

MCP: the vendor-documented endpoint is per-store (https://yourstore.com/wp-json/mcp/mcp-adapter-default-server) and the integration is a developer preview; official_mcp_server cites the vendor docs URL rather than a fixed endpoint. The legacy /wp-json/woocommerce/mcp endpoint was removed in WooCommerce 11.3 and now returns HTTP 410.

Community MCP servers: searches were restricted to site:woocommerce.com and the GITHUB REPOSITORIES / MCP REGISTRY sections were empty, so no community MCP server URLs were verified; this field is not evidence that none exist.

Sandbox: sandbox_or_test_env=true reflects documented local development stores (Studio CLI/wp-env), not a hosted sandbox for the core REST API. The only hosted sandbox found is sandbox.woocommerce.com for the Woo Marketplace SaaS Billing API, which requires business review before access is granted.

SDK officialness: the docs list Java, .NET, and Android libraries separately and note 'contact the respective authors', suggesting they are third-party; only JavaScript, PHP, Python, and Ruby were treated as vendor-maintained.
Rate limits: no rate limits are documented for the core WC REST API v3; only the Store API has optional, disabled-by-default rate limiting.
Composio catalog returned zero items for the query 'WooCommerce' (total_items: 0), which seems surprising for a major ecommerce platform - worth re-checking the catalog query or alternate naming.
